author: Ash

copy.intro: You've found the Lucky Brand cut that works for you, and now you'd like a second pair from somewhere else. Maybe cheaper, maybe in a petite length. These 15 denim brands are the ones people name in Lucky's place, heritage labels like Levi's and Lee alongside Los Angeles makers like Joe's and Miss Me. The most-named come first, and among equals, the ones priced closest to Lucky go higher.

bodies.levis:
Levi's is the first stop if you like Lucky for its American denim roots, because it's where a lot of that story starts. The company dates to 1853 in San Francisco, and it still makes jeans, casual wear and accessories for men, women and kids.

Levi's has stores in 40 US states and about 3,300 stores and shop-in-shops worldwide, so trying a fit on in person is usually easy. Buckle stocks it too, with the Levi's Cinch Baggy Wide Leg Jean ($84.95) among its women's jeans.

If you'd rather order online with free shipping on any order and a long return window, Silver Jeans Co. is set up better for that.
bodies.true-religion:
True Religion is the pick if you want Lucky's California denim background with a designer label on it. It started in 2002 and is based in El Segundo, California, and its own store pages sell it as designer jeans.

There are True Religion shops in 24 US states, including California and New York, plus Canada and Mexico. So you can see the fits in person before you commit.

If you'd like a California label with prices you can compare first, Miss Me starts at $88 and Joe's Jeans at $168.
bodies.lee:
Lee is where to go for workwear-rooted American denim with a longer history than Lucky's. It began in 1889 in Salina, Kansas, added a zipper fly in the 1920s, and its Lazy S back pocket has been the official Lee pocket since 1944. So that back-pocket stitch is the quick way to spot a pair.

There are Lee stores in 22 US states. And there's a family link on the way. Kontoor Brands announced in May 2026 that it would sell Lee to Authentic Brands Group, which owns the Lucky Brand name.

Lee shares a parent company and a Greensboro, North Carolina, headquarters with Wrangler. If the western side of Lucky is what you like, look at both.
bodies.madewell:
Madewell is the closest match if you want Lucky's denim-first focus with far more fits to choose from. Its own pitch is premium denim, and $148 buys most of its women's jeans, with the dearest pair at $198. That's a step up from Lucky's full-price $129.

The fit range is the reason to pay it. Madewell sells petite, tall, curvy and plus fits, and plus runs from 14W to 24W, where Lucky's women's waists stop at 35. Its Denim Atelier does one-on-one fitting and tailoring, and Insiders get free hemming in store.

You get 30 days to send things back, where Lucky gives you 60. J.Crew, from the same parent company, sells its jeans at the same $148 to $198 with more western details in the range.
bodies.gap:
Gap is the cheaper way into everyday jeans from a brand with denim in its history. It started in San Francisco in 1969, and its women's jeans run $79.95 to $99.95, so even the top of the range comes in under Lucky's full price. If you wear Lucky's flares, the High Rise '70s Flare ($89.95) is a good place to start.

Sizes run 000 to 20, with petite and tall versions and short, regular and long inseams. Free shipping starts at $50 for Gap Good Rewards members, and it's free to join. And you can walk into a Gap in 46 states.

Returns run 30 days, half of Lucky's 60, so try things on soon after they arrive.
bodies.miss-me:
Miss Me is the pick if the embellished side of Lucky is what you're after. The Los Angeles label started in 2001 and builds its line around statement denim, from rhinestone-studded throwbacks to cleaner modern cuts. The Lilia Bootcut Jeans ($94) come in under Lucky's full price, while the Bandit Baggy Wide Jeans ($149) sit just above it.

Most styles come in waists 23 to 34 with a choice of 30, 32 or 34-inch inseams, so you pick the length instead of hemming it later. Buckle carries the brand as well, including the Universal Boot Stretch Jean ($129).

The 30-day return window starts when your order ships, so open the box quickly. Free US shipping starts at $150.
bodies.scotch-soda:
Scotch & Soda gives you Lucky-level prices with a European point of view. It was founded in Amsterdam in 1985, and its full-price women's jeans run $108 to $178. So the Essentials The Sky Straight Jeans ($108) cost less than Lucky's $129, and The Wave Super Wide Leg Denim ($178) costs more.

Waists go from 24 to 34, and each pair is sold by waist and inseam (30, 32 or 34), so the length is settled before it ships. US delivery is free over $200, a much higher bar than Lucky's $85.

Returns run 30 days from receipt. If free shipping on a single pair matters more than the look, Silver Jeans Co. is the easier order.
bodies.buckle:
Buckle is the store to visit if you'd like to compare several denim brands in one trip, because denim is its biggest category. Its own BKE label hangs next to Miss Me, Levi's, Wrangler and 7 For All Mankind. Prices run from the Very J High Rise Wide Leg Jean ($54.99) to the 7 For All Mankind Dojo Trouser Stretch Jean ($308).

There are 440 stores across 42 states. Waists on the styles it lists run 22 to 38, past Lucky's 35. Returns take 60 days, the same as Lucky, and they're free in store or $6.99 by mail.

With that many labels on one rack, check each brand's own size chart rather than assuming one Buckle size fits across them.
bodies.naked-and-famous:
Naked & Famous sells raw denim that you fade yourself, the opposite of a broken-in pair. The Montreal label cuts and sews in Canada from Japanese denim and skips washes and distressing completely.

Prices start at $141, so the Bestie in Black Lightweight Denim ($143) is a small step up from Lucky's $129, and the heavier selvedge pairs climb toward $495. Sizes cover a 23 waist in the women's cuts up to 44 in the men's, wider than Lucky's women's 24 to 35. Hemming is free, and US shipping costs a flat $10.

Before you order, know that refunds come as store credit rather than money back. And at the top end, its heavy selvedge pairs cost more than anything else on this list.
bodies.j-crew:
J.Crew is worth a look if you like Lucky's western touches but need a different length. Its women's jeans run $148 to $198, and the range includes a western straight jean with metallic studs and an embellished lowrider ($188).

You can buy most pairs in Classic, Petite or Tall lengths, and waists reach 37, two sizes beyond Lucky's women's 35. That makes it one of the better options here if Lucky's inseams never quite land.

Shipping is the drawback. Standard delivery costs $7 unless you're a J.Crew Rewards member, and $7.50 comes off a refund when you use the prepaid return label. Madewell, its sister brand, sells at the same prices and adds plus sizes.
bodies.silver-jeans-co:
Silver Jeans Co. is the cheaper pick that also makes ordering online painless. Full-price jeans run $88 to $108, so the Avery Straight Leg Jeans ($94) or the Tuesday Baggy Wide Leg Jeans ($104) come in under Lucky's $129.

Standard shipping is free on every order, with no minimum, and returns are free for 45 days after delivery. Women's sizes run 22 to 36, or 00 to 16 in dress sizes, and there are petite and plus sections, which Lucky's women's range doesn't have.

If you'd rather try on before you buy, Gap's prices are close and its stores cover 46 states.
bodies.joes-jeans:
Joe's Jeans is the step up if you like Lucky's Los Angeles denim and want to put more of your budget into fit. Joe Dahan started it in LA in 2001 and is still its creative director, and the brand pitches itself on putting fit first. Full-price jeans start with The Hi Honey bootcut ($168) and go up to The Harlowe Studded ($328).

Waists run 23 to 34, and many cuts come in a petite version, which Lucky's women's range lacks. Ground shipping is free over $200, and returns are 30 days from delivery, with $7 taken off if you use the prepaid label.

It also ships to Canada, the UK, France, Mexico and Australia, handy if you're buying for someone abroad.
bodies.american-eagle:
American Eagle is the mall pick if curvy fits are the priority. Its women's jeans come in Classic and Curvy fits, and many of its cuts have a curvy version, such as the Super High-Waisted Baggy Wide-Leg.

The terms line up well with Lucky's. Returns run 60 days, the same window, and US shipping is free over $75, a little under Lucky's $85. An online return costs $5, though Level 3 Real Rewards members and AE cardmembers don't pay it.

It was founded in 1977 and is based in Pittsburgh. If you want a curvy fit with more embellishment, Miss Me is the better match.
bodies.guess:
Guess is the other Los Angeles denim label to try if you like Lucky's California roots. The Marciano brothers started it in 1981, nine years before Lucky, and its women's jeans cover straight, mom, wide, skinny, bootcut and flare cuts.

Its stores are in eight states, including California, Texas, Florida and New York, so check the locator before you plan a trip. There's a small link to Lucky in the ownership too: Authentic Brands Group owns 51% of Guess and also owns the Lucky Brand name.

If you'd like a California label you can try on in more places, True Religion has stores in 24 states.
bodies.wrangler:
Wrangler is where to go if the western side of Lucky's Americana is the part you love. Its jeans were designed for rodeo use, and the 13MWZ, a men's western jean introduced in 1947, is still on sale. The store has its own Western Collection as well.

There are Wrangler stores in 22 states, and Buckle carries the brand, so trying a pair on is easy. Like Lee, it belongs to Kontoor Brands, and it won the Professional Rodeo Cowboys Association's official endorsement in 1974.

For a dressier take on western denim with a price on the tag, J.Crew's studded western straight jean is the alternative.

closing.heading: How to choose
closing.body:
Start with budget. Under Lucky's $129, Gap ($79.95 to $99.95) and Silver Jeans Co. ($88 to $108) are the cheapest full-price jeans here, and Silver adds free shipping and 45-day returns. For about the same money, Miss Me and Scotch & Soda sit on either side of $129, Miss Me for embellishment and Scotch & Soda for cleaner European cuts.

If fit is the problem, Madewell and J.Crew cost more but cover petite and tall, and Madewell adds plus. To try on in person, Levi's and Gap have stores in 40-plus states, and Buckle puts several brands on one rack. And if the western side is the draw, go to Wrangler. For raw denim you fade yourself, Naked & Famous is the only one here that does it.

faqs.a: Authentic Brands Group owns the Lucky Brand name. Catalyst Brands, formed when JCPenney and SPARC Group merged, runs the business as its licensee, including sourcing, wholesale and the North American stores.
